about: When each Mars landing happened on Mars (spacecraft event time, UTC): the instant sites-v1.json holds and the 3D view goes to. A time published as received on Earth is turned back by the one-way light time from the view's own ephemeris (almanac-ephem.js _ephBodyJ2000), which gives NASA's published event times for Phoenix, InSight, Curiosity and Perseverance to 1 s.

sources.NSSDCA: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive, mission pages (Viking 1 and 2 landers, Mars Pathfinder): landing times UT
sources.JPL-PHX: NASA/JPL Phoenix landing press kit and release, 2008-05-25: touchdown 23:38:24 UTC spacecraft time (signal received 23:53:44)
sources.JPL-MSL: NASA/JPL Mars Science Laboratory landing press kit: touchdown 2012-08-06 05:17:57 UTC spacecraft time (05:31:45 Earth-received)
sources.JPL-INS: NASA/JPL InSight landing release, 2018-11-26: touchdown 19:52:59 UTC Earth-received, 19:44:52 spacecraft time
sources.JPL-MER: NASA/JPL MER landing releases: Spirit 2004-01-04 04:35 UTC and Opportunity 2004-01-25 05:05 UTC, Earth-received
sources.JPL-M20: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 landing press kit: 3:55 p.m. EST (20:55:00 UTC) Earth-received; one-way light time 11 min 22 s
sources.CNSA-EDL: Wei et al. 2022, Tianwen-1 Mars entry vehicle trajectory and atmosphere reconstruction preliminary analysis, Astrodynamics 6(1) 81-91, doi:10.1007/s42064-021-0116-y: 'landed ... on May 15, 2021, at 7:18 (UTC+8)'; Hu et al. 2022, Astrodynamics 6(1) 27-37, doi:10.1007/s42064-021-0124-y: '7:18 AM BJT'

events.why: Earth-received 04:35 to the minute, less 568.7 s of light time
Earth-received 05:05 to the minute, less 663.9 s of light time

Published to the minute. The time of the landing itself: both papers reconstruct the entry from the vehicle's own measurements (IMU, air data), whose clock is the vehicle's; the signal (17 min 43 s of light time that night) reached Earth near 23:36
